issues.description: raise PerformanceWarning followed by an unreachable break — dead code that proves nobody read the diff
issues.detail: Look at the loop body: `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` and then `break` on the next line. The break is unreachable. Either you meant to `warnings.warn` and continue, or you meant to raise and the break is leftover garbage. Pick one. Dead code in a 20-line patch is a bad sign.

issues.description: raising a class named PerformanceWarning instead of warning with it is wrong-shape
issues.detail: A class called `PerformanceWarning` is a warning. You're raising it as an exception to abort the write. That is a category error: the name lies about the behavior. Either rename it to an Error and raise, or call `warnings.warn` and let the user proceed. The test even asserts `pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning, ...)` which cements the bad shape.

issues.description: safe_chunk_size uses np.prod of shape tuple, not bytes-per-element times elements — wrong math
issues.detail: `np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * max(1, z.dtype.itemsize)` — `zarr_write_chunks` is a tuple of per-axis sizes. For a 1-D shape that happens to be elements; for N-D it's the total element count, which is what you want, but `max(1, itemsize)` is suspicious — when would itemsize be 0? You're papering over a case that can't happen. Just write `z.dtype.itemsize * int(np.prod(zarr_write_chunks))` and be done.

issues.description: only axis 0's first chunk is checked; the modulo test assumes uniform chunks across all axes
issues.detail: The loop iterates axes but only inspects `dw[0]`, the first chunk on each axis. `normalize_chunks` can return uneven tail chunks, and the check ignores them. For a real correctness gate, check that every chunk on the axis is divisible by the shard size, or document why first-chunk is sufficient. Right now the comment-free heuristic will silently miss misalignment.

issues.description: `not x % y == 0` is bad taste — write `x % y != 0`
issues.detail: Operator precedence here happens to work because `==` binds tighter than `not`, but a reader has to stop and check. `if x % y != 0:` is what you mean. This is the kind of cleverness that wastes the next maintainer's time for zero benefit.

issues.description: PR description asks an open design question — patch isn't ready
issues.detail: The author writes: "What should we do when there's competition between the global config and shard shape? Would an exception be appropriate here?" That's not a PR, that's an RFC. Decide the policy first, then submit the patch that implements it. Right now the code answers "raise" and the description asks "should we raise?" — those don't match.

review.summary: The idea — use shard shape as `previous_chunks` so `auto_chunks` produces shard-aligned larger chunks — is good taste. The implementation is not ready. There's literal dead code (a `break` after a `raise`), a class named `PerformanceWarning` being raised as a fatal error, and `safe_chunk_size` math with a defensive `max(1, itemsize)` that hides whatever the author was actually worried about. The divisibility check inspects only the first chunk per axis. And the PR description openly asks whether raising is the right call while the code already raises — decide the policy, then submit. NEEDS-WORK. Fix the dead break, pick warn-or-raise and name the class accordingly, clean up the size calculation, and check all chunks on the axis, not just `dw[0]`.
